title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: A Guide for Quantitative Analyst Salary
description: Learn how to convert a quantitative analyst salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and casual loading explained with Fair Work and ABS data.
salarySummary: A quantitative analyst earning $64.50 per hour (the ABS average for Professionals) working 38 hours a week would have an annual gross pay of approximately $127,452 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time employee on a 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. This method assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the difference between award rates and the National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries and occupations and are often higher. For example, the Children’s Services Award and Pharmacy Award have had increases due to gender undervaluation reviews. Always check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830, meaning super is only calculated on earnings up to that amount. For a quantitative analyst earning $127,452 annually, the super contribution would be $127,452 × 12% = $15,294.24 per year, added to your total remuneration.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly-to-Annual Conversion

When you know your hourly rate, converting it to an annual figure helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax and super. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full-time employees, the typical week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Act and used in the National Employment Standards. This article assumes a 38-hour week unless stated otherwise. If you work part-time or different hours, simply replace the 38 with your usual weekly hours.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the standard for full-time work in most awards and the National Minimum Wage. The 52-week year accounts for all weeks in a calendar year, including paid leave. If you are paid fortnightly, you can also calculate your fortnightly pay as weekly pay × 2. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, weekly pay is $1,004.90 and fortnightly pay is $2,009.80.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage increased to $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award minimum wages rose by 4.75% on the same date. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements.

Award rates vary by industry and occupation. For instance, the Children’s Services Award and Pharmacy Award have had additional increases due to the Fair Work Commission’s gender undervaluation review. Always check the specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Quantitative Analyst Salary: What the Data Shows

A quantitative analyst is a specialised role typically classified under the Professionals occupation group. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Employee Earnings and Hours survey for May 2025, the average hourly total cash earnings for non-managerial Professionals was $64.50. Using the 38-hour week conversion:

**$64.50 × 38 × 52 = $127,452 per year**

This is a useful benchmark for a quantitative analyst salary. For comparison, the ABS also reports that average weekly total cash earnings for all full-time adult ordinary time employees (a broader measure) was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $54.83 per hour. The higher figure for Professionals reflects the specialised skills and demand for quantitative roles.

It is important to note that these are averages; actual quantitative analyst salaries can vary based on experience, location, and employer. The ABS data also shows that the most common method of setting pay is individual arrangement (38.5% of employees), followed by collective agreement (34.6%). Award-only coverage is only 22.7% of employees, so many quantitative analysts negotiate their own rates.

### Casual Loading and Your Salary

If you work as a casual quantitative analyst, your employer must pay a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is not an extra benefit but compensates for the lack of paid sick leave and annual leave. For a casual quantitative analyst, the effective hourly rate would be $64.50 × 1.25 = $80.63, leading to an annual gross of $80.63 × 38 × 52 = $159,364. However, this is before tax and super, and you would not receive paid leave.

## Tax and Super: What Comes Off the Top

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Additionally, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. For a quantitative analyst earning $127,452, the tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $82,452 ($45,001–$127,452) = $24,735.60
- Total tax ≈ $28,755.60, plus Medicare levy of $2,549.04, giving a total of about $31,304.64.

Your take-home pay would be roughly $96,147 per year, or $1,849 per week. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

Superannuation Guarantee is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $127,452 salary, the super contribution is $15,294.24 per year. This is not deducted from your pay but is an additional cost to your employer. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet for Your Own Calculation

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember, the tool assumes a 38-hour week and the standard tax and super rules. It does not account for penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

For a quick reference, see our [reference tables](/data) for common hourly rates and their annual equivalents. If you are comparing job offers, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page explains how to evaluate total remuneration including super and benefits.

## Summary

Converting an hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. For a quantitative analyst salary, the ABS average of $64.50 per hour gives an annual gross of $127,452. Always check the relevant award or agreement, and remember that casual loading adds 25% on top. Tax and super are calculated separately, with super paid on top of your gross. Use the tools and guides on this site to get a clearer picture of your earnings.
